note: Hand-picked recent AI reporting from large, reputable newsrooms, links verified. Source mix is limited by access tooling: WSJ, Reuters, FT and Bloomberg are blocked from automated browsing, so the openable/verified set skews CNBC, AP (wire) and MIT Technology Review. The updater (8×/day) can broaden sources over time.

items.title: 'Model fatigue' sets in as AI labs race to roll out new versions at frenetic pace
items.blurb: Anthropic, OpenAI, Meta and Google all shipped updates in one week; users and enterprises struggle to keep up.

items.title: AI data centers are transforming rural land markets — and fueling a backlash
items.blurb: Wall Street's compute buildout is inflating rural land prices, splitting farm communities between windfall sellers and organized opposition.

items.title: Meet the CISO: A new front line star in the AI cybersecurity war
items.blurb: After the OpenAI-Hugging Face agent hack, AI threats push chief information security officers into the boardroom.

items.title: U.S., China gear up for mid-September AI safety talks: Reuters
items.blurb: First bilateral AI-safety dialogue since frontier-model tensions rose; Treasury's Bessent to lead, though the White House hedged on timing.

items.title: A 'shakeout' in early-stage AI may be coming as VC money gets pickier on valuations
items.blurb: Venture investors are tightening on early-stage AI pricing, a signal for how durable the funding boom is.

items.title: Goldman just revised this credit-market forecast thanks to the AI sector
items.blurb: Goldman lifts 2026 investment-grade issuance forecast to $2.3 trillion; AI-related borrowers account for about a quarter of supply.

items.title: Nvidia's investments grow to $99 billion as chip giant expands its reach
items.blurb: Nvidia's stakes across AI startups and infrastructure now near $100 billion, deepening its role as financier of its own demand.

items.title: AI models are becoming unknowable
items.blurb: Frontier systems like Astra increasingly resist interpretation, complicating safety review and regulator oversight of how models reach answers.

items.title: Why Nvidia's 'defensive move' to acquire Hugging Face is about much more than chips
items.blurb: Analysts read the $12.9B deal as protecting the open-model ecosystem that drives Nvidia chip demand from rivals.

items.title: Behind the Curtain: AI creators race to understand their creations
items.blurb: Labs concede interpretability lags capability as systems approach thresholds their own builders cannot fully explain.

items.title: The Download: selling battlefield drone data and AI reshaping language
items.blurb: Ukraine begins selling drone-flight datasets to contractors, opening a commercial market in combat training data.

items.title: U.S. auto safety regulator opens probe into nearly 1,000 Tesla Cybercabs
items.blurb: NHTSA audits Tesla's self-certification of a robotaxi with no steering wheel, pedals or mirrors as commercial service begins.

items.title: Tesla's Cybercab now available for ride-hailing
items.blurb: Tesla puts wheel-free two-seater Cybercabs into commercial service in Austin, a milestone for AI-driven autonomy at scale.

items.title: Axios interview: Sam Altman's sobering siren
items.blurb: Altman says the next model generation will be "sobering" and that alignment progress will now pace releases.

items.title: OpenAI begins rolling out Astra model after warning of its advanced cyber capabilities
items.blurb: GPT-6 Astra ships in phases, starting with vetted Daybreak security customers before ChatGPT paid tiers, the API and AWS.

items.title: OpenAI releases new model GPT-6 Astra, says it may represent AGI
items.blurb: OpenAI positions Astra as a milestone in its AGI push; president Greg Brockman calls it the start of the AGI era.

items.title: Altman raises stakes on government scrutiny as AI advances
items.blurb: Altman calls the administration's voluntary Astra review productive and says Congress still lacks a basic frontier-AI framework.

items.title: Scaling agentic AI pilots across the enterprise
items.blurb: Roughly 80% of Fortune 500 firms have adopted agentic AI, but most remain stuck in isolated pilots rather than production scale.

items.title: Reply to: Limited benchmarks constrain the conclusions of a general-purpose versus clinical AI comparison
items.blurb: Nature Medicine exchange over whether general-purpose models genuinely outperform purpose-built clinical AI on real clinical queries.

items.title: Hidden China risks are emerging in America's multibillion-dollar AI data center boom
items.blurb: Chinese-made transformers, switchgear and batteries sit deep in the US data-center power stack as capacity heads toward 152 GW.

items.title: Nvidia agrees to buy Hugging Face for almost $13 billion, expanding up the AI stack
items.blurb: Nvidia's second-largest acquisition puts the dominant open-model hub, used by 18 million developers, under a chipmaker.

items.title: Bernie Sanders floats ban on superintelligent AI
items.blurb: First prominent US legislator to seek an outright permanent ban on superintelligence, plus a pause on frontier development.

items.title: The Download: rethinking child safety and fossil-fueled farming
items.blurb: Daily briefing covering online child-safety policy rethinks as AI-generated content pressures existing protection frameworks.

items.title: Brain implants, like Elon Musk's Neuralink, fuel China-U.S. bioscience rivalry
items.blurb: AI-assisted neural decoding is shortening device calibration times, turning brain-computer interfaces into a US-China competitive front.
